items.title: FDS victims' families want full crash report released transparently
items.summary: KUCHING: Families of the victims of the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Ulu Baram, want the full investigation report released transparently, without being concealed or politicised. Muhammad Faiz Abdul Malek, husband of medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, said investigators had informed the families that the findings were preliminary. He said the families had been told that the full investigation report could take between one and two years to complete.

items.title: Knife seized in investigation into woman's alleged murder
items.summary: Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the weapon was found after the suspect himself pointed it out during an inspection at the scene. However, he said an examination at the scene found stab wounds to the left side of the victim's abdomen and her right cheek. He said preliminary investigations indicated that the incident was believed to have stemmed from marital discord.

items.title: Pearly–Thinaah break new ground in Denmark
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Women's pair Pearly Tan–M. Thinaah were made to work before reaching their first Denmark Open semi-final on Friday. The breakthrough saw Pearly–Thinaah surpass their previous best showing at the Super 750 tournament, a quarter-final appearance in 2024.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - October 16, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Here are today's top stories. Minimum starting salary The proposed legal changes follow the government's announcement under the 2027 Budget of a RM2,500 minimum starting salary framework for graduates and semi-skilled workers. Enough is enough Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) passengers want stronger security measures after an attempted cable theft along the Kajang MRT line from Phileo Damansara to the Damansara town centre was disrupted this morning, following a suspected cable theft attempt.

items.title: Jetour shifts gears from SUVs to global travel lifestyle
items.summary: CHINESE automotive brand Jetour is expanding its push into the global travel lifestyle market, combining sport utility vehicles (SUVs), off-road technology and conservation initiatives under its "Travel+" strategy. Jetour said its cumulative global sales reached 2.56 million units as of September this year, with vehicles available in more than 100 countries and regions. The brand will showcase its technology and travel-focused strategy at the 2026 Jetour Global Technology Experience Day, themed "Future Travel Starts Now", from Oct 20-23.

items.title: When banking products converge, experience becomes the differentiator
items.summary: Unlike a product feature, experience depends on data, processes and people working as one. Across Asean, core banking products - savings accounts, cards, loans and digital services look increasingly alike. Twimbit's forthcoming Asean Banking Titans 2026 research benchmarking leading banks across the region finds that on core journeys such as account opening or moving money, top banks are separated by narrow margins.

items.title: Onn Hafiz calls Asean meeting as Johor records 53rd day of haze
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi has called for an emergency Asean meeting and stronger regional cooperation to tackle transboundary haze, as the state recorded its 53rd day of haze since Aug 25. He said regional cooperation must be strengthened in fire prevention, hotspot monitoring and firefighting efforts to prevent further haze episodes. Pasir Gudang recorded an Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 198, approaching the very unhealthy threshold of 201.

items.title: Two TNB contractors suffer third-degree burns in Tebrau substation incident
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Two Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) contractors suffered third-degree burns after being electrocuted during maintenance work at a substation in Kangkar Tebrau. The incident occurred around 6.10pm at the Kangkar Tebrau main intake substation in the Tebrau 4 Industrial Area. It also triggered power disruptions in more than 10 residential areas across the city, including Taman Johor Jaya, Taman Molek, Adda Heights, Bandar Dato' Onn, Austin, Eko Flora, Cascadia, Kempas, Setia Tropika, Taman Gaya, Senai and Taman Pelangi Indah.

items.title: Zahid says Malaysia ready to help Indonesia fight forest fires after Prabowo accepts foreign aid
items.summary: TIANJIN, Oct 16 — Malaysia is ready to help Indonesia tackle widespread forest and land fires after President Prabowo Subianto agreed to accept offers of assistance from neighbouring countries. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said Malaysia welcomed the Indonesian government’s openness to receiving foreign assistance to fight the fires. “We are grateful to the Indonesian government and President Prabowo for being open to accepting foreign assistance to tackle the forest fires.

items.title: Loke: RTD to fully cooperate in probe into fatal Senawang crash
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Road Transport Department (JPJ) will cooperate with the police to ensure a thorough and transparent investigation into a crash that killed one of its personnel and seriously injured another near the Senawang exit on the North-South Expressway last night. Transport Minister Anthony Loke said action would be taken against any party found to have violated the law or committed misconduct. Loke extended his condolences to the family of Negri Sembilan RTD Enforcement Assistant Grade KP2 Mohd Azrul Rashid Yaakub, who was killed in the accident while on duty.

items.title: Johor Baru power outage: Substation fire in Tebrau disrupts electricity supply
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Firefighters are battling a blaze at an electrical substation in the Tebrau 4 Industrial Area in Jalan Kangkar Tebrau here, with several nearby areas experiencing power outages. The Johor Fire and Rescue Department said it received an emergency call at 6.10pm, with firefighters from the Tebrau Fire and Rescue station arriving at the scene six minutes later. Eight firefighters and a fire engine were deployed to tackle the blaze.

items.title: Perlis MACC recovers nearly RM700,000 through forfeitures since 2024
items.summary: ARAU, Oct 16 — The Perlis Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has recovered RM698,255.55 through forfeitures from 2024 to date. Perlis MACC director Mohd Nor Adha Ab Gani said the state anti-graft agency opened 65 investigation papers (IPs), recorded 84 arrests and brought 37 charges to court during the period. Mohd Nor Adha said Perlis MACC also focused on preventive measures, submitting 61 Governance Improvement Recommendations to federal and state departments and statutory bodies.

items.title: Cape EMS ties up with Taiwan's FIC Global unit
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Cape EMS Bhd has signed a memorandum of agreement (MoA) with Taiwan's FIC Global Inc unit Pro3C (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd to support the latter's expansion in Johor's artificial intelligence (AI) manufacturing supply chain. The agreement, signed on Oct 16, positions Cape EMS as Pro3C's local strategic partner, providing manufacturing infrastructure, supply chain management, facilities and operational support. The collaboration supports Cape's CEB 2.0 transformation, aimed at improving facility utilisation, generating recurring revenue and shifting its electronics manufacturing services (EMS) business towards higher-value manufacturing.

items.title: Govt supports efforts to strengthen Islamic scholarship, says Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government supports efforts to strengthen Islamic scholarship, research and intellectual discourse to contribute to national governance and the well-being of the ummah, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. In a post on X, Anwar said this after receiving a courtesy call today from a delegation from Tuanku Syed Sirajuddin International Islamic University (UniSIRAJ), led by its board chairman, Perlis Mufti Datuk Dr Mohd Asri Zainul Abidin. Anwar said the meeting also discussed a proposal to organise the International Seminar on al-Qaradawi Thought next year to broaden discourse on Islamic thought and contemporary national governance challenges.

items.title: China tells Trump's press secretary to visit 'more often' after toilet comments
items.summary: BEIJING: Beijing told White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia on Friday to visit China "more often" after she said the country lacked "proper toilets" less than a week into her new post. Zacharia, who previously lived in China and is due to visit next month, recalled in an interview the perception in 2016 that China would soon overtake the United States. "I remember this very distinctly, having just come from China, thinking, 'How is China the next country on the horizon?

items.title: MBI Selangor subsidiaries form strategic alliance to explore dark fibre network 2.0
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Smartsel Sdn Bhd and Pengurusan Air Selangor Sdn Bhd (Air Selangor), key subsidiaries of Menteri Besar Selangor (Incorporation) (MBI Selangor), will explore the proposed Selangor Dark Fibre Network 2.0, which aims to leverage existing utility corridors to deploy high-capacity fibre networks. The partnership combines Air Selangor's water utility infrastructure with Smartsel's digital infrastructure and technology capabilities to develop digital connectivity and intelligent infrastructure across the state. MBI Selangor group chief executive officer Datuk Ts Saipolyazan M Yusop said the collaboration aimed to translate group synergy into commercial opportunities and greater value for Selangor.

items.title: El Niño could hit fishermen, fish farms as temperatures soar to 40°C, says Mat Sabu
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Oct 16 — Coastal fishermen and aquaculture operators could be hit if El Niño pushes temperatures up to 40°Celsius, prompting calls for early preparations to protect the country’s food production. Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said the phenomenon could drive fish farther out to sea, posing a challenge for coastal fishermen who lack the capacity to fish in deeper waters. He said the government had discussed preparations for El Niño with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim as part of efforts to strengthen national food security.

items.title: Pasir Gudang blaze extinguished after 43 hours
items.summary: PASIR GUDANG: A fire involving piles of timber and buoys in Jalan Muhibbah, Kampung Pasir Putih, here, was fully extinguished yesterday after nearly 43 hours of firefighting. The blaze, which broke out at 10.04pm on Oct 14, engulfed 1.3935ha of open land before firefighters extinguished it at 4.47pm yesterday. Johor Fire and Rescue Department operations commander Nazarudin Yusof said firefighters had contained 98 per cent of the blaze by 8am yesterday , covering about 148,000 sq ft, before continuing efforts to put out the remaining hotspots.

items.title: Two TNB contractors critically injured by electric shock as substation fire triggers Johor Bahru blackout (VIDEO)
items.summary: The incident triggered a fire and disrupted electricity supply in parts of Johor Bahru. TNB said the fire broke out at 6.03pm, interrupting power supply in several areas around Johor Jaya and its surrounding areas. The Johor Fire and Rescue Department said the Tebrau fire station received a distress call about the incident at 6.10pm.

items.title: Families of children killed in Pakistan school roof collapse demand justice
items.summary: PESHAWAR: The families of children killed when a school roof collapsed in northwest Pakistan called for "justice" on Friday, a day after more than 30 pupils and a teacher were crushed to death. "The parents of all these children must receive justice," tailor Muhammad Wahab, who lost his 11-year-old nephew Hammad in the accident, told AFP on Friday. Dozens of people gathered outside the school on Friday to mourn the children killed in the collapse, which officials blamed on dilapidated infrastructure.

items.title: UM student who questioned Najib donations faces online harassment, threats
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A Universiti Malaya (UM) student leader who questioned public donations to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak has faced online harassment and threats after videos of her remarks went viral. Ummi Umairah Bakhit, 23, said she would not be intimidated by the attacks, adding that she believed it was her responsibility to challenge public perceptions, particularly among young people. Ummi, who is also a member of the UM Student Union, said her questions were relevant as the forum had also focused on transformation.

items.title: Malaysia ready to help Indonesia fight forest fires, says Zahid
items.summary: TIANJIN (CHINA): Malaysia is ready to assist Indonesia in tackling widespread forest and land fires after President Prabowo Subianto agreed to accept offers of aid from neighbouring countries. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said Malaysia welcomed Indonesia's willingness to receive foreign assistance and remained committed to helping its neighbour, in the spirit of friendship and strong bilateral ties. "Even though the help we have offered is small, Malaysia is prepared to send aid to assist our neighbour," he said, adding that Malaysia values Prabowo's openness on the matter.

items.title: Malaysia on track to exceed 2026 GDP growth forecast — Economists
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is on track to exceed the official full-year gross domestic product (GDP) growth expectation of 4.8 to 5.3 per cent after the economy expanded by 5.5 per cent in the first nine months of 2026, said economists. The Finance Ministry, in its Economic Outlook 2027 report, has raised its 2026 real GDP growth projections to 4.8 to 5.3 per cent, up from 4.0 to 4.5 per cent in Budget 2026. "With growth hitting 5.5 per cent in the first three quarters, the economy is on track to exceed the full-year official 4.8–5.3 per cent GDP growth expectation," he told Bernama.

items.title: Indian police detain 'cockroach' movement founder Dipke ahead of protest
items.summary: NEW DELHI: Police detained Abhijeet Dipke, founder of India's 'Cockroach' movement, on Friday, according to live footage shared by his group, ahead of a protest he had called in the capital's central business district. The youth-led 'Cockroach Janta Party' (CJP), opposition groups and student organisations have held almost daily protests this month demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over a revision of voter lists that critics say favours Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). Earlier on Friday, police met Dipke and warned him against going ahead with the protest.

items.title: AAIB flags firefighting gaps at Sarawak airstrip after crash killed five
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — The Air Accidents Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has urged the operator of Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Port (STOLport) in Miri, Sarawak, to review its rescue and firefighting arrangements after a helicopter crash killed five people, including four Health Ministry personnel, on September 8. The AAIB recommended that aerodrome operator Malaysia Airports Sdn Bhd (MASB) review rescue and firefighting arrangements across its STOLports to ensure auxiliary personnel were properly trained and equipped, and that firefighting equipment and personal protective equipment (PPE) were properly maintained and serviceable. The bureau said the recommendation followed findings that Malaysia Volunteers Corps Department (Rela) personnel assigned to auxiliary rescue and firefighting duties had responded to the blaze without appropriate firefighting PPE.

items.title: Malaysian suspected of running RM7.2mil agarwood scam
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A Malaysian is suspected of masterminding an agarwood investment scam involving more than HK$14 million (RM7.2 million) that was uncovered by Hong Kong police on Wednesday. The other five suspects were Hong Kong residents. He said they had invested between HK$30,000 (RM15,565) and HK$1.9 million (RM985,800) in schemes offered by a Hong Kong-based company since 2017.

items.title: Haze watch: 29 areas recording unhealthy or worse air, Larkin, Pasir Gudang API hits 202
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — Air quality in Larkin and Pasir Gudang, Johor, deteriorated to very unhealthy levels this evening, with the Air Pollutant Index (API) reaching 202 as at 5.30pm, while 27 other areas nationwide recorded unhealthy readings. According to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, six other areas in Johor recorded unhealthy API readings, namely Pengerang (181), Batu Pahat and Kota Tinggi (171 each), Kluang (168), Tangkak (159) and Segamat (156). Three stations in Negeri Sembilan also recorded unhealthy readings: Nilai (181), Seremban (174) and Port Dickson (170).

items.title: Fatal Senawang crash: Lorry rammed into JPJ car during roadside inspection, police say
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Oct 16 — A lorry carrying dry food products lost control and crashed into a Road Transport Department (JPJ) car and another lorry during a roadside inspection, killing a JPJ officer and injuring three others on the North-South Expressway near Senawang, police said today. Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the two JPJ personnel had been inspecting a motoloader carrying a cabin load on the emergency lane at Kilometre 256.1 northbound when the lorry approached from behind at about 10.30pm yesterday. The 42-year-old JPJ officer suffered head injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene.

items.title: Man, 67, bludgeoned to death in Permas Jaya; suspect arrested
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: A 67-year-old man was found dead with head injuries after being repeatedly beaten with a blunt object in Permas Jaya, here, yesterday. Johor Baru (Selatan) deputy police chief Superintendent Ng Swie Chait said the victim also suffered injuries to his face and arms. Ng said police seized an iron walking stick and a framed portrait to assist investigations.

items.title: Death in lock-up: Family lodges report against KL police chief
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: The family of the late Noorizwan Zulkefly, 42, lodged a police report against Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus here today over his remarks on the death of the detainee. Lawyer Latheefa Koya said the report was prompted by Fadil's statements on Noorizwan's death, which she described as dishonest and an attempt to justify the incident on the grounds that the deceased had a criminal record. In the report, Latheefa said Fadil's statements at the press conference had failed to address the severe injuries found on Noorizwan's body, as documented in the forensic findings.

items.title: MARKET PULSE PM OCT 16, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia closed lower on Friday as buying interest shifted from index heavyweights to smaller-cap technology and telecommunications stocks as well as real estate investment trusts. In the cryptocurrency market, Bitcoin rose to RM335,213. jw7BtEbsUZw © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: ‘They were aware’: Bukit Aman on five Malaysians held in Tokyo with cocaine in their shoes
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 16 — Five Malaysians arrested for concealing five kilograms of cocaine in their shoe soles at Haneda International Airport in Tokyo, Japan, on October 10 are believed to have been drug mules paid RM8,000 each. Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the suspects, aged between 19 and 26, were each given the shoes by a drug syndicate that is still being identified. He said police were investigating whether all the suspects were directly involved in the syndicate and whether they had previously travelled to other countries using the same modus operandi.

items.title: Teenage girl sacrifices schooling as both parents battle stage four cancer
items.summary: Her mother, Noor Diana Hashim, 47, was diagnosed with breast cancer, which has now spread to her liver, lungs, spine and neck. Her father, — 47-year-old Iman Heart nasyid band frontman Zek Ayry Khan Zarak Khan — has nasopharyngeal cancer. Noor Diana needs to undergo chemotherapy as soon as possible.

items.title: RM2,000 minimum wage backed by economic data, nationwide consultations
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The proposed RM2,000 minimum wage was determined through economic research and extensive consultations with employers, workers and academics, rather than an arbitrary decision, National Wages Consultative Council chairman Tan Sri Zainal Rahim Seman said. He said the council had conducted 21 engagement sessions nationwide and commissioned a comprehensive study to ensure the proposed rate was fair to workers without placing undue pressure on employers. The study, supported by a government allocation of between RM1 million and RM1.5 million, examined several economic indicators to determine an appropriate minimum wage.

items.title: Malaysia banks on policy certainty, economic resilience to attract investment – Amir Hamzah
items.summary: BANGKOK: Malaysia is strengthening its business environment, policy certainty and economic resilience to attract long-term investment, with foreign and domestic direct investments reaching record highs, said Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan. "Malaysia's story is resilience," he said at the Bloomberg Global Policy Series: ASEAN Growth Markets Spotlight – Competing and Connecting for Global Capital here on Friday. Amir Hamzah said Malaysia was also focused on moving its economy up the value chain by strengthening key industries, including semiconductors, and deepening domestic supply chains to create higher-value jobs and enhance its competitiveness in global trade.

items.title: Petronas, Petrovietnam deepen energy cooperation under new pact
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) and Vietnam National Industry–Energy Group (Petrovietnam) have signed a strategic alliance agreement to strengthen cooperation across the energy value chain. It was signed at Petrovietnam's headquarters by Petronas president and group chief executive officer Tan Sri Tengku Muhammad Taufik and Petrovietnam president and chief executive officer Le Manh Cuong. In a statement, Petronas said it remained committed to supporting Vietnam's evolving energy needs while exploring broader opportunities for regional energy cooperation.

items.title: Wet and windy: MetMalaysia warns of thunderstorms in 11 states and Putrajaya until 8pm
items.summary: In Kedah, the affected areas include Kubang Pasu, Sik, Baling, Kuala Muda, Langkawi and Padang Terap, while in Perak, the weather alert covers Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Larut, Matang and Selama, Kerian, Kinta, Perak Tengah, Manjung, Hilir Perak and Bagan Datuk. In Kelantan, the warning covers Gua Musang, Kuala Krai, Jeli, Tanah Merah and Machang, while in Terengganu, it affects Kemaman, Dungun and Hulu Terengganu. In Pahang, the areas involved are Jerantut and Kuantan, while in Selangor, they comprise Petaling, Klang, Kuala Selangor, Kuala Langat, Sepang, Sabak Bernam and Hulu Langat, alongside Tampin in Negeri Sembilan.

items.title: Transport minister vows action if negligence found in Senawang fatal crash involving JPJ officers
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 16 — The Road Transport Department (JPJ) will provide full cooperation to the Royal Malaysia Police to ensure that investigations into the accident that claimed the life of one of its personnel at KM256 of the North-South Expressway, near the Senawang exit last night, are conducted thoroughly and transparently. Transport Minister Anthony Loke said appropriate action would be taken against any party found to have violated the law or committed misconduct or negligence, based on the investigation findings. Loke expressed deep sorrow and extended his condolences to the family of Negeri Sembilan JPJ Enforcement Assistant Grade KP2 Mohd Azrul Rashid Yaakub, who was killed in the accident while on duty.

items.title: Subang-Laos drug jet: Cops await Philippine confirmation on politician's role
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Police are awaiting confirmation from the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA) on claims that a Filipino politician funded the charter of a private jet used to transport 521kg of syabu from Subang to Laos. Federal Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said police had identified two Filipinos who booked the private jet. "The Philippine syndicate hired private aviation services to transport drugs from Laos to the Philippines.

items.title: Want OKU status? Here’s how the Welfare Dept evaluates applications
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 16 — The registration of persons with disabilities (OKU) follows the OKU Registration Guidelines (2019 Amendment), jointly developed by the Social Welfare Department (JKM) and the Health Ministry. In a statement today, JKM said the process also involves medical specialists who sit on the OKU Registration Committee under the National Council for Persons with Disabilities. Medical officers, practitioners or specialists assess an individual’s functionality and disability using the OKU Registration Application Form (BPPOKU Amendment 2/2019), it said.

items.title: Govt overpaid Semantan Estate up to RM500,000 for Duta Enclave land, property valuer tells court
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — The High Court was told today that the Malaysian Government had overpaid Semantan Estate Sdn Bhd (1952) between RM400,000 and RM500,000 in compensation for the acquisition of 263.272 acres of land known as the Duta Enclave in 1956. “If the court accepts my valuation, no additional compensation should be paid to the plaintiff (Semantan Estate),” he said. In earlier proceedings, Tan testified that the government paid Semantan Estate RM1.39 million in compensation in 1965, exceeding his recommended amount.

items.title: PeKa B40 becomes PeKa Sihat in healthcare revamp as govt looks to ease clinic queues
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — The Health Ministry’s PeKa B40 healthcare programme will be rebranded as PeKa Sihat, with changes aimed at making the initiative more effective and easing congestion at public health clinics, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today. “The Cabinet has agreed to the proposed amendments to the PeKa B40 programme under the Health Ministry, taking into account of its effectiveness in tackling non-communicable diseases. Fahmi said the Health Ministry would announce further details of the rebranded PeKa Sihat programme.

items.title: Italian cyclist targeted by stone-throwing teens while camping in Sabah
items.summary: RANAU, Oct 16 — Police have launched an investigation into a viral video showing a group of teenagers allegedly throwing stones at an Italian cyclist who was camping at Kampung Lohan while on a solo cycling expedition around Sabah. Ranau District Police Chief Supt Mursalin Mahmud said a special team had been formed to investigate the incident after the video attracted public attention. The cyclist, Nicola Chiacchio, had stopped at the Kampung Lohan field during his journey around Sabah using a bicycle.

items.title: Splitting the AG’s two hats: Azalina takes charge of talks with select committee
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — Law and Institutional Reform Minister Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said has been tasked with engaging a Parliamentary Special Select Committee on constitutional amendments to separate the roles of the Attorney General and the Public Prosecutor. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim made the announcement after a decree by the Malay Rulers on the proposed amendments at the recent Conference of Rulers meeting, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today. “The prime minister has instructed Datuk Seri Azalina to conduct the engagements and discussions with the Parliamentary Special Select Committee, which has already prepared a draft for the constitutional amendments,” Fahmi said at the weekly post-Cabinet media briefing, which was broadcast live.

items.title: Fahmi: No Malaysian palm oil companies involved in burning activities in Indonesia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — There are no Malaysian plantation companies with palm oil concessions in Indonesia that were involved in forest fires linked to the regional haze issue, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. He said this was based on cross-reference checks conducted with local companies that maintain palm oil concessions in Indonesia. “The Malaysian Palm Oil Board (MPOB) will continue to have engagement sessions with Malaysian plantation companies that have their operations in Indonesia,” he said.

items.title: Human Resources Ministry to introduce Starting Basic Salary Guidelines in June 2027 rollout
items.summary: Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the Starting Basic Salary Guidelines based on the Malaysian Standard Classification of Occupations (Masco) would provide more comprehensive starting basic salary benchmarks according to job types and qualification levels. For graduate-level jobs, Ramanan said Kesuma had proposed salary benchmarks for Masco categories 1 to 3, covering graduates with degrees, diplomas and Malaysian Advanced Skills Diplomas at Level 5. “For semi-skilled jobs, Kesuma will align this approach with the Skills-Based Starting Basic Salary Guidelines.

items.title: Pakatan confident of Melaka win, but Amirudin says voters will decide
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is confident of winning the upcoming Melaka state election, while acknowledging that the outcome ultimately rests with voters. The coalition’s election director, Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari, said PH would announce its candidates for the state election on Oct 24, after he finalises the list with the coalition’s president and top party leaders. Yesterday, PH communications director Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said discussions on candidates for the Melaka state election were over 95 per cent complete.

items.title: Malaysia unveils six homegrown chips worth RM300m as it shifts from making to designing semiconductors
items.summary: Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Nasir said the six innovations demonstrated the growing capabilities of Malaysian companies, although further work was needed to secure customers, meet industry qualification requirements and turn the designs into commercially successful products. The innovations were developed by companies operating within the Malaysia Semiconductor IC Design Park, with applications ranging from artificial intelligence (AI) and automotive electronics to satellites and autonomous drones. Akmal said Malaysia was building on its established strengths in semiconductor packaging, testing and related manufacturing activities, while expanding into integrated circuit (IC) design through partnerships, talent development and investment.

items.title: Children’s Court closes case of five teenage girls accused of verbally abusing Zara Qairina, submissions set for Nov 16
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 16 — The case involving five teenage girls charged with allegedly uttering abusive words against Zara Qairina Mahathir at the Children’s Court has closed, with submissions scheduled for November 16. Counsel Joan Goh, who represents one of the teenagers, said the court had fixed November 30 for the reply submissions, followed by clarification on December 4 before a date would be set for the ruling on whether a prima facie case had been established. She said more than 20 witnesses had testified during the hearing, but not all child witnesses testified in the Children’s Court and Zara’s mother had also not taken the stand.

items.title: Heavy downpour triggers flash floods across Kuching, roads and Sarawak Plaza basement swamped
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 16 — Several areas in Kuching were hit by flash floods following heavy rain this afternoon. Flooding was reported at Sarawak Plaza, the Mile 3 underpass, Jalan Tun Jugah and Jalan Batu Lintang after the rain began at around 1.30pm. As of 2.45pm, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) had forecast thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in several parts of Sarawak until 7pm.

items.title: ‘Until he retracts, go away’: Tuanku Muhriz rebukes Negeri Sembilan MB in public
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — The Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, publicly reprimanded Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim as the state’s constitutional crisis drags on. Videos circulating on social media show the ruler telling a group of people that Ismail had written to the Keeper of the Rulers’ Seal to say that Tuanku Muhriz was no longer the state’s Yang Dipertuan Besar. A visibly angry Tuanku Muhriz then asked why the menteri besar wanted an audience with him.

items.title: Malaysia’s fury rises as Indonesian haze shuts schools, blankets region, and sparks calls for accountability
items.summary: Indonesian wildfire haze has caused a regional pollution crisis and prompted growing frustration in neighbours, including Malaysia. “Malaysia and Indonesia are close neighbours, but that relationship must also come with responsibility,” Malaysian parliamentarian Syerleena Abdul Rashid told AFP. she said.

items.title: Khazanah and PNB channelled nearly RM40m into FashionValet in 2018, court hears in Vivy Yusof trial
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — The Sessions Court here was told today that local fashion company, Fashion Valet Sdn Bhd (Fashion Valet), received investment funds totalling nearly RM40 million from Khazanah Nasional Berhad (Khazanah) and Permodalan Nasional Berhad (PNB) eight years ago. Tay Lay Hong, 54, a banking services manager at the Bukit Damansara branch of Public Bank, said the funds were deposited into a Public Bank account belonging to Fashion Valet through four separate transactions between March and December 2018. Tay also confirmed that a sum of RM11 million was withdrawn from Fashion Valet’s bank account on August 21, 2018, via an online ‘bulk payment’ transaction.

items.title: AAIB releases preliminary report on Long Lellang helicopter crash that killed five
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — The Air Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has published its preliminary report into the September 8 crash of a Flying Doctor Service helicopter at the Long Lellang STOLport in Miri, Sarawak, which killed a pilot and four passengers. The Transport Ministry said the Bolkow BO105 S helicopter, registered 9M-LLF and operated by Layang-Layang Aerospace Sdn Bhd, was on a scheduled Flying Doctor Service flight from Selungo to the Long Lellang STOLport at the time of the accident. It said the report compiles the factual information identified at the early stage of the investigation, in line with the government’s commitment to transparency and accountability.

items.title: Sarawak gives RM100,000 each to families of Flying Doctor Service crash victims
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 16 — The Sarawak state government has contributed RM100,000 to each of the families of the five victims of the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Baram, which occurred on September 8. Additionally, educational assistance is being provided through Yayasan Sarawak (Sarawak Foundation) to help ease the burden on the victims’ families, specifically by ensuring the continuity of their children’s education. The contributions were presented by Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg to the next-of-kin of the five victims during a handover ceremony held at the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly complex today.

items.title: Lawyers urge public to avoid speculation as Zara Qairina inquest heads to January ruling
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 16 — Lawyers involved in the inquest into the death of Zara Qairina Mahathir have urged the public to avoid speculation and allow the judicial process to take its course following the conclusion of witness testimonies. Lawyer Joan Goh, who represents one of the teenagers accused in the bullying case involving the Form One student, said she hoped the evidence presented during the inquest had been addressed comprehensively. “The coroner also sought feedback and recommendations from all parties on improving future inquest proceedings, including school safety and investigation procedures,” he said.

items.title: Police confirm AKPS officer killed in KLIA quarters domestic dispute, knife seized, husband remanded
items.summary: Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said police received a report regarding the incident at about 9.30pm after a man surrendered himself at the Bandar Baru Salak Tinggi Police Station in Sepang, Selangor, and reported his wife’s death at their residence. Acting on the information, a police team was dispatched to the scene, where they found a woman, in her 30s, unconscious. He said initial investigations by the Negeri Sembilan D10 Forensic Division found that the victim sustained injuries suspected to be from being stabbed, while a knife along with several other pieces of evidence were also seized to assist in the investigation.

items.title: China agrees in principle to Malaysia’s proposal for world TVET council, says Zahid
items.summary: TIANJIN, Oct 16 — China has agreed in principle to Malaysia’s proposal to establish a World Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) Council, said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. He noted that the proposal to establish the World TVET Council, with China acting as the permanent secretariat, was formally presented during his keynote address at the World Technical and Vocational Education and Training Development Conference 2026 (WVTEDC 2026) here today. In terms of principle, Deputy Prime Minister Ding and China’s Minister of Education have agreed,” he said during a press conference following the event.

items.title: Tuanku Muhriz bestows state honours on three Undangs and their consorts
items.summary: The Negeri Sembilan State Secretary’s Office said in a statement today that the three Undangs - Datuk Klana Petra Muhammad Faris Johari of Luak Sungei Ujong, Datuk Mendika Menteri Akhirulzaman Datuk Azrin Khairi of Luak Jelebu and Datuk Sedia Raja Hassan Ab Hamid of Luak Rembau — were conferred the Darjah Tertinggi Negeri Sembilan (DTNS). Also present at the ceremony were the Tunku Ampuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Aishah Rohani Tengku Besar Mahmud, Tunku Besar Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin Tuanku Muhriz, and Tunku Panglima Besar Tunku Zain Al-‘Abidin. Other attendees included State Secretary Datuk Mohd Zafir Ibrahim, State Legal Adviser Datuk Muzalmah Mustapha Kamal and State Financial Officer Datuk Masri Razali.
